references.text: Joshua obeyed Moses' command to go out and fight against Amalek, as mentioned in the previous verse
Joshua was appointed as Moses' successor and here early showed his obedience and leadership
Hur is mentioned together with Aaron as leaders of the people while Moses was away
Hur was the grandfather of Bezalel, the craftsman who built the tabernacle
Amalek attacked Israel, and this was remembered as an event that required retribution
Amalek was a descendant of Esau, and this explains the historical enmity
Joshua, as Moses' servant, later became the leader of Israel after Moses' death
Saul received command to punish Amalek for what they did to Israel when they came up from Egypt
Highlights Joshua's consistent role as Moses' closest assistant in both military and religious missions.
Contrasts and complements the picture of who has access to God's presence on the mountain in different situations.
Shows the development of Joshua from an active helper in battle to a formal successor through the Lord's plan.
Confirms the theological interpretation of Moses' and Aaron's role as intercessory priests during the war event.
